Rendered reports from the DeltaGain analyses. Each page is generated from a `REPORT.md`
that lives beside the code that produced it, in
[`analysis/`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/tree/main/analysis) — the page and
the source therefore cannot drift.

These are working analyses. Every result is computational; nothing here has been
expressed, assayed or otherwise tested at the bench, and each report states its own
limitations.

## Available

### [Delta Gain: findings synthesis](delta_gain/index.html)

The novelty-yield measurement this project is named for: how much new protein-level
information newly annotated fungal genomes add beyond UniProt and RefSeq. Whole-proteome
funnel, what the surviving clusters are, family-level diversity against an order-matched
null, and species accumulation across 23,567 genomes. Reproduced verbatim from the pipeline
repository at a pinned commit.

**One result on it has since been qualified** — see the box at the top of the page, and its
companion below.

Source: [1KFG/delta-gain](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain) @ [`91eb5fe`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain/blob/91eb5fe6be888707fcf9c6953ef68a99bd91d414/docs/FINDINGS.md)

### [The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition](y1000_deposition/index.html)

A companion test to the funnel's largest family-level effect. 1,033 genomes from two
UW-Madison Y1000+ BioProjects — 5.8 % of the new side — carry about three quarters of the
enriched families' novelty, because their proteins went to Figshare rather than to the
protein databases the baseline is built from. Counting them as known inverts the effect.
The random-Pfam controls barely move, which is what makes it a confound rather than a
correction to everything.

Source: [`analysis/delta_gain_funnel/`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/tree/main/analysis/delta_gain_funnel)

### [Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes](upo_clades/index.html)

A census of 97,520 PF01328 proteins, phylogenetic placement onto a 187-leaf reference
tree, and a candidate list for expression. The report is as specific about what the
model cannot do as about what it can: finding active-site residues is validated 95/95,
ranking clade-V-like pockets works for ordering candidates, and predicting whether an
arbitrary protein is an active peroxygenase **is not reliable** — out-of-clade AUC 0.556
on the 19 characterized enzymes the field has. It also reports four attempts to lift that
ceiling that failed their own tests, and two errors found in the underlying genome
database.

Source: [`analysis/enzymes_UPO/`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/tree/main/analysis/enzymes_UPO)

### [Candidate effectors of two *Mucor* strains isolated from *Marchantia*](mucor_secretome.html)

This analysis has moved to the MorenoLab repository. This page now carries a short public
summary and a link to the new location. The full analysis is lab-only until the paper is
published.

### [Fungal pigments: carotenoid, melanin and mycosporine pathways](pigments.html)

A chapter on the four curated pigment knowledge bases: steps, evidence tiers per pathway,
review errors that were caught, and the owner decisions that block a census. **No gene
census has been run**; the chapter reports no gene counts. Under the strict evidence rule no
carotenoid route and no complete DHN route is above tier T3. The fungal mycosporine
references come from one species, *Phaffia rhodozyma*.

Source: [`analysis/pathway_census/PIGMENTS.md`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/blob/main/analysis/pathway_census/PIGMENTS.md)

### [Pathway knowledge base and the metabolite corpus](pathway_corpus.html)

A record of what was tried when carotenoid, melanin and mycosporine pathways were curated
as evidence-tiered tables and compared with the GNPS-processed metabolite corpus. The
comparison was **not run**: the pre-set detectability gate failed for carotenoids,
melanin, fucose and fungal MAAs (0 of 84 fungal-reference accessions show the main
carotenoids). The page lists the failed design (mass shifts), the data errors that review
caught, hypothesis status, and twelve rules for connecting the corpus to other data.
Curation is unfinished and no step set has had owner review; corpus counts are reported by
the EBC agent, not re-measured here.

Source: [`analysis/pathway_census/REPORT.md`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/blob/main/analysis/pathway_census/REPORT.md)

### [Carotenoid biosynthesis genes in 23,376 BFD fungal genomes](pathway_carotenoid/index.html)

The first census result for the carotenoid pathway: 14 step HMMs, the score check that
sets each cutoff, a search of 244,451,335 proteins, and what a lower cutoff would add.
**It reports search hits, not genes.** Tree placement was run for one step only, and the
5 reference proteins of that step lie inside a clade that holds 98.6 % of the candidates (10,708 of 10,863), so
the placement cannot yet tell candidates apart. Every output is stamped `PROVISIONAL`. The
page lists the negative results and what was not done.

Source: [`analysis/pathway_census/reports/carotenoid/`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/tree/main/analysis/pathway_census/reports/carotenoid)

### [DHN and L-DOPA melanin genes in 23,376 BFD fungal genomes](pathway_melanin/index.html)

Search, tree placement and gain and loss for the DHN and L-DOPA melanin steps, with a
per-species comparison of the two pathways. Several calls are close to search hits and
`tyrosinase` carries most of the L-DOPA signal. Every output is stamped `PROVISIONAL`.

Source: [`analysis/pathway_census/reports/melanin/`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/tree/main/analysis/pathway_census/reports/melanin)

### [Mycosporine genes in 23,376 BFD fungal genomes](pathway_mycosporine/index.html)

Search, tree placement and gain and loss for three mycosporine steps (`ddgs`, `omt`,
`atp_grasp_ligase`). No step has a verified fungal reference. Every output is stamped `PROVISIONAL`.

Source: [`analysis/pathway_census/reports/mycosporine/`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/tree/main/analysis/pathway_census/reports/mycosporine)

## Not published here

Work that is in the repository but has no page here:

- **The BFD gene-model and annotation findings** —
  [`analysis/enzymes_UPO/bfd_findings/`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/tree/main/analysis/enzymes_UPO/bfd_findings).
  Summarized in §6 of the UPO report above. It has no page of its own because its main
  result — that the start/stop-codon completeness flags are wrong database-wide — was
  fixed upstream the same day it was found, so its tables describe a snapshot that is
  being rebuilt, and its most interesting observation (≈2,265 ascomycete proteins placing
  in a basidiomycete clade) is explicitly unresolved pending a test the report specifies
  but does not run.

- **The antiSMASH subset work** —
  [`analysis/bgc_subset/`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/tree/main/analysis/bgc_subset).
  Scripts and `FINDINGS.md` for running antiSMASH 8.0.4 on BFD genomes and keeping only the
  tables a compound-to-cluster analysis needs (32 genomes, 13 species so far). It has no
  page because the run is a pilot, and the database form of a cluster is not decided.
